newsitem.title: UK: Middle East tankers steady, slightly down to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Middle East tankers steady, slightly down to Japan.

text.p: Middle East crude tanker rates were generally steady on Monday, although some brokers detected softness in very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Japan.
"There are quite a few Eastern ships about. Japanese companies tend to go for Japanese ships and that has been pushing rates down a little," one broker said.
He put VLCCS to Japan at about W65, slightly down from W67.5 on Friday, but brokers said other Middle East rates were flat.
Middle East/west VLCCs continued to be fixed at W55, with trips to Singapore remaining at about W57.5. Inter-U.K./Cont rates for 80,000 tonners firmed to W120-125 from W115.
"We're seeing a gradual improvement (for 80,000 tonners) with some charterers quite stuck for loading at the end of the month," an Italian broker said.

For cross-Med cargoes he said there was little activity on the 80,000 tonne side but some fresh enquiry for million-barrel (130,000-tonne) vessels. He said rates for both sizes were "quite stable" at around W100 and W90 respectively.
There was little activity on the transatlantic market, which continued at W62.5 for VLCCs and W95 for million-barrel ships.
Likewise, West Africa-U.S. Gulf trips were steady at W62.5 for VLCCs and W95 for million-barrel ships.
On fuel oil, 25,000 tonnes cross-Med was steady at W180 while the same quantity inter-U.K./Cont was assessed slightly lower at W195 from W200.

For 70,000 tonnes of crude Caribs/upcoast the market was slightly softer, at about W165 from W175. "There has been an increase in (availability of) Aframaxes for early February. Anyone who has a cargo will be shooting for W165 or less," a U.S. broker said.
Fuel oil was down to W185-190 from W200 for 50,000-tonne cargoes due to plenty of available tonnage, he added.
